question: What is Apple's most recent macOS security update as of today, which systems does it affect, and which actively exploited issues does Apple identify?

claims.text: Apple's security-releases index says the latest version of macOS is 26.6.2 and lists macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 with a release date of August 17, 2026.

evidence_passages.text: As of August 27, 2026, Apple’s security-releases index says “The latest version of macOS is 26.6.2” and lists `macOS Tahoe 26.6.2` with a release date of August 17, 2026.

claims.text: Apple's security-content page for macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 says the update was released August 17, 2026 and is available for macOS Tahoe.

evidence_passages.text: Apple’s security-content page for `macOS Tahoe 26.6.2` says the update was released August 17, 2026 and is “Available for: macOS Tahoe.”

claims.text: In the supplied Apple-page evidence for macOS Tahoe 26.6.2, Apple does not identify any actively exploited issues.
acceptable_patterns: does not identify any actively exploited issue

evidence_passages.text: I found no Apple statement on either page identifying any actively exploited issue in macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 or Safari 26.6.1. This is an inference from absence: on the two Apple security-content pages above, Apple lists the CVEs and impacts, but the pages do not include Apple’s usual exploitation wording such as “Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been actively exploited.”

**Actively Exploited CVEs:** None reported

The security document does not include any CVEs marked with "Apple is aware of a report that this issue may have been exploited."

rejected_claims.text: Safari 26.6.1 is Apple's most recent macOS security update.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence marks Safari 26.6.1 as a newer Mac-related security release, but the question asks for the most recent macOS security update and the same evidence says the latest version of macOS is 26.6.2.

rejected_claims.text: Apple identifies CVE-2026-65400 as actively exploited in its most recent macOS security update.
rejected_claims.reason: Unsupported by the supplied Apple evidence. Active-exploitation reporting in the supplied material is tied to third-party reporting about macOS Tahoe 26.6.1, not to Apple identifying an actively exploited issue in macOS Tahoe 26.6.2.

rejected_claims.text: Apple says there were no actively exploited Apple security issues affecting Macs at all.
rejected_claims.reason: Overly broad and time-unstable. The supplied evidence only supports that Apple does not identify actively exploited issues on the cited pages for macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 and Safari 26.6.1.

rejected_claims.text: Apple's macOS Tahoe 26.6.2 security page lists fixes in Audio, ImageIO, IOGPUFamily, Kernel, WebKit, WebKit History, and WebKit Storage.
rejected_claims.reason: Non corroboré et motifs de notation invalides. La liste des composants (Audio, ImageIO, IOGPUFamily, Kernel, WebKit, WebKit History, WebKit Storage) ne provient que du résumé auto-rapporté du run Codex, dont les tool_results indiquent que la charge utile des recherches n'est pas exposée et dont opened_urls est vide ; le run Claude, qui a réellement récupéré https://support.apple.com/en-us/148281, ne rapporte que le nombre de CVE (30) sans aucun de ces composants. De plus, les acceptable_patterns 'Audio', 'Kernel' et 'WebKit' sont des sous-chaînes génériques non discriminantes ('WebKit' matche à l'intérieur de 'WebKit History'/'WebKit Storage'), tandis que l'exigence simultanée des sept composants est trop étroite pour une notation lexicale déterministe.
